subject: english
chapter_title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

concepts.title: The Inauguration of a Democratic South Africa
concepts.definition: On 10 May 1994 leaders and dignitaries gathered at the Union Buildings amphitheatre in Pretoria for the inauguration of South Africa's first democratic, non-racial government, with military generals saluting Mandela, once a prisoner.
concepts.key_idea: The sight of jets trailing smoke in the colours of the new flag and generals who would have arrested him saluting him marks the triumph of justice over apartheid.
question_patterns: where and when did the inauguration ceremony take place
why did military generals salute mandela at the inauguration
what pledge did mandela take at the ceremony
describe the scene of the inauguration of the new government
who became the first black president of south africa
what do the smoke trails of the jets stand for

solution_steps.explain: Check the details: 10 May, the Union Buildings amphitheatre, Pretoria, with international leaders present.
Generals who would once have jailed Mandela now salute him; jets trail the new flag's colours.
The two deputies pledged to obey and uphold the Constitution and devote themselves to the well being of the republic.

concepts.title: Apartheid and Mandela's Idea of Courage
concepts.definition: Apartheid was a system of racial segregation that brutalised South Africa, and Mandela says courage is not the absence of fear but the triumph over it, learned from those who fought oppression.
concepts.key_idea: Mandela counts himself the sum of all those who sacrificed before him, and defines the brave man as one who conquers fear rather than one who never feels it.
question_patterns: what does courage mean to mandela
which system of segregation did south africa practise
who does mandela thank for his attainment of freedom
why does mandela call himself the sum of all african patriots
is the brave man without fear according to mandela
what was the greatest wealth of mandela's country

solution_steps.explain: Identify apartheid as political and social separation by race that created white domination.
Courage means not being overcome by fear; fear can be conquered, not abolished.
Mandela sees himself as the product of countless martyrs and heroes, the sum of all African patriots.

concepts.title: Twin Obligations to Family and Country
concepts.definition: Every person carries twin obligations: one to the family, parents, wife and children, and another to the people, community and country, and Mandela could not fulfil the first without betraying the second under apartheid.
concepts.key_idea: Honouring family duties brought him isolation as a young man, so he was forced to weigh his people's freedom against personal life.
question_patterns: what twin obligations does every man have according to mandela
how did apartheid interfere with mandela's family obligations
what happened to mandela when he honoured his family obligation
why was mandela separated from his family in the struggle
explain the two kinds of duty described by mandela
could mandela serve both his family and his people at once

solution_steps.explain: Family duty covers parents, wife and children; public duty covers people, community and country.
The regime twisted family duty into betrayal of the people, forcing him into isolation from home.
Mandela kept the people's freedom first, which cost him family life and personal liberty.

concepts.title: Transitory Freedoms and Basic Honourable Freedoms
concepts.definition: As a boy Mandela enjoyed transitory freedoms of running in fields, swimming and roasting mealies, while as a student he hungered for basic honourable freedoms of earning his keep, marrying and living where he chose.
concepts.key_idea: Gradually he saw that his boyhood freedom was an illusion: when he learnt his birth hid chains, his hunger for freedom became the desire for his people's liberty.
question_patterns: what did being free mean to mandela as a boy and as a student
distinguish transitory freedoms from basic and honourable freedoms
what boyhood freedoms does mandela recall
when did mandela realise his freedom was an illusion
why did mandela join the african national congress
what is the hunger for freedom that mandela describes

solution_steps.explain: Running in fields, swimming in streams, roasting mealies and riding bulls, unaware of chains.
Earning a livelihood, marrying, having a family and living with dignity wherever one chooses.
Discovering that his birth hid chains turned the personal desire for freedom into a longing for his people's liberty.

concepts.title: The Oppressor and the Oppressed Are Both Robbed
concepts.definition: Mandela holds that the oppressor and the oppressed alike are robbed of humanity: the prisoner loses freedom while the oppressor loses his humanity, and both must be set free.
concepts.key_idea: No one is born hating another person; people learn to hate, and if they can learn to hate, they can be taught to love, for love comes more naturally to the human heart.
question_patterns: does mandela think the oppressor is free why or why not
how are both the oppressed and the oppressor robbed of humanity
which does mandela think is natural to love or to hate
explain the idea that love comes more naturally to the human heart
why does the oppressor need to be set free
how can a person learn to love according to mandela

solution_steps.explain: The oppressed lose freedom and dignity; the oppressor takes another's freedom and thereby loses their own humanity.
Hate is learned, so it can be unlearned, and love is the truer instinct of the human heart.
Both oppressor and oppressed must be liberated for a free nation to exist.
